title: Legal Assistant - Conveyancing
description:
Location: Totnes, Devon

Contract Type: Permanent

Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience - Circa £24 to £28k

Hours: Monday to Friday

Working Pattern: Office-based

Contract: Full-time

Experienced Legal Assistant sought to join the Residential Property team of a well-regarded and established law firm in South Devon.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Conveyancing Legal Assistant who has a good understanding of the residential conveyancing process from instruction through to post-completion and is looking to join a friendly, supportive and collaborative team.

Position Overview

Working closely with the firm's Residential Property lawyers, you will provide comprehensive support across a busy conveyancing caseload and assist with transactions throughout the conveyancing process.

Responsibilities will include:
- Dealing with new client instructions and initial enquiries
- Preparing estimates and client care documentation
- Assisting with client onboarding, including source of funds requirements
- Preparing and issuing contract packs
- Obtaining property searches
- Liaising regularly with clients by telephone and email
- Supporting matters through exchange of contracts
- Preparing completion statements
- Assisting with completions, including obtaining mortgage funds and sending completion monies
- Handling post-completion administration
- Preparing and submitting SDLT returns
- Dealing with Land Registry applications and registrations
- Maintaining accurate files and progressing matters efficiently
- Working closely with fee earners and the wider Residential Property team

The role would suit someone who enjoys being involved throughout the conveyancing process rather than undertaking purely administrative duties and who is confident working within a busy property department.

Requirements
- Previous experience working as a Legal Assistant within Residential Conveyancing
- Good understanding of the conveyancing process from initial instruction through to completion and post-completion
- Experience with client onboarding and source of funds requirements
- Experience preparing contract packs, searches and completion statements
- Knowledge of SDLT and Land Registry/post-completion procedures
- Excellent client care and interpersonal skills
- Confident communicating with clients by telephone and email
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
- Ability to prioritise effectively within a busy environment
- Good IT skills and confidence using case management systems
- Friendly, professional and collaborative approach

Benefits
- Competitive salary and benefits package
- Enhanced annual leave entitlement
- Additional holiday for long service
- Company pension
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Mental health and wellbeing support
- Free annual flu vaccinations
- Coaching and mentoring
- Modern and comfortable office environment
- Regular social events and team activities
- Firm-wide away days
- Staff discounts on legal services
- Supportive and inclusive working culture
- Long-term career development within an established firm

This is a great opportunity for an experienced Conveyancing Legal Assistant seeking a stable, permanent position within a friendly and highly regarded Residential Property team, based in the heart of Totnes.

title: Reception/Administrator
description: We are looking for someone with excellent communication and interpersonal skills, who can engage with patients in a professional, compassionate and empathetic manner. The ideal candidate will be resilient, adaptable, and able to manage competing demands while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail. A positive, team-focused attitude and a genuine commitment to patient care are key to succeeding in this role. Whilst previous administrative or reception experience is desirable, we are also keen to hear from applicants with limited or no direct experience, as this minimum 12-month maternity cover position provides an excellent opportunity to develop administrative, communication and patient-facing skills within a busy GP practice. We are seeking a confident, proactive, and highly organised Administrator to join our busy GP practice team. This is a fast-paced and dynamic front-line role, where no two days are the same, and the ability to stay calm under pressure is essential. As the first point of contact for our patients, you will pay a vital role in creating a welcoming, respectful and efficient environment. The working pattern for this fixed term 12-month maternity cover (full time) is as follows:- Monday 8.15am - 5.15pm (with 1 hour lunch break) Tuesday 8.15am - 5.15pm (with 1 hour lunch break) Wednesday 8.15am - 12.15pm Thursday 8.15am - 6.30pm (with 1 1/4 hours lunch break) Friday 8.15am - 5.15pm (with 1 hour lunch break) Starting pay of £12.71 per hour. On successful completion of probationary period this will increase to £12.81 per hour. Closing date Friday 16th October. Successful applicants will be contacted by the end of the working day on 19th October at the latest. Interviews are planned for Wednesday 21st and Thursday 22nd October. The interview process will include group interviews on the Wednesday and formal interviews on the Thursday for those short listed following the group stage. Job Title: Healthcare Administrator to the Nursing Team REPORTS TO: Healthcare Administration Manager/Deputy HOURS: 37 hours per week Job Summary The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way by telephone and on the helpdesk Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the Practice including the provision of clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the Practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and Responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the Practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the Healthcare Admin Manager, Deputy, Practice Manager, dependent on current and evolving Practice workload and staffing levels: Maintaining security in accordance with Practice protocols Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Taking messages and passing on information Filing and retrieving paperwork Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with Practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Clearing and re-stock consulting rooms as required Assist in preparation & setting up of the working environment & nursing clinical rooms for appropriate procedures & maintaining the organisation of them Set up clinic templates on to the IT system Co-ordinating the ordering & maintaining supplies used within the nursing team Providing clerical assistance to Practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Ordering, re-ordering and monitoring of stationery and other supplies Dealing with clinical waste in line with practice health and safety policy Keeping the reception areas, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Attending departmental meetings Other duties as required by the line manager Underpinning Policies Confidentiality: Adhere to the General Data Protection Regulations (GDPR) May 2018. In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk and contribute to the practice risk register as needed Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate This job description may be subject to change from time to time to reflect the changing needs of the Practice, but it is a correct reflection of the type of duties that need to be undertaken. Litchdon Mission Statement Providing quality healthcare by valuing both patients and staff in a supportive and sustainable environment. Litchdon Values Compassionate Care We treat staff, patients, carers, and relatives with kindness, respect, and dignity, fostering a culture of mutual empathy. Holistic wellbeing We prioritise the physical, mental, and emotional wellbeing of our staff which then enables them to deliver person centred care. Positive reliable teams We cultivate professional, approachable, and cohesive teams built on loyalty, trust, and mutual respect, enabling them to deliver safe and effective care to patients. Family focussed We support the work-life balance of our staff and recognise the importance of family for patients and colleagues alike. Innovation and Growth We embrace change, prioritise sustainability, and nurture professional development across the workforce to improve processes and patient care. Environmental Responsibility We are mindful and committed to be as eco-friendly as possible by ensuring we consider the impact of our practice on both the community and the planet. title: Receptionist
description: As a Medical Receptionist, you will be the first point of contact for our patients and visitors. You will work within a busy and dynamic reception team to deliver a high-quality and professional front-line service in line with practice policies and procedures. First point of contact for patients in person, on the phone, and electronically. A varied and interesting role working with a great team. Key Responsibilities Reception Duties Greet patients and visitors warmly and respond to enquiries efficiently. Manage appointments using System One Guide new and temporary patients through registration procedures. Take payments as required and issue receipts. Handle incoming and outgoing post. Open and close the premises when rota requires. Assist with general admin tasks including photocopying, printing, and document handling. Telephone Duties Answer and manage incoming calls promptly and professionally. Administrative & Specific Duties Process repeat and acute prescription requests. Complete daily Pathlink allocation, process emails, and manage uncollected scripts. Perform monthly script returns and manage script records. Order stationery and printer supplies. Bradninch site only Manage prescription payments and handouts. You must be able to work at our main site in Cullompton and provide cover at our branch sites when required. Hours available include a mix of early mornings and late finishes, shared fairly across the team. On-the-job training and mentoring included.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for someone to join our excellent reception team who all work very hard at being the first point of contact for the majority of patients. The role is demanding, and sometimes difficult, but overall rewarding. The whole Practice Team are friendly and we look forward to welcoming a new member of staff. This is a part-time post working Monday 07:45 - 17:00 as well as both Tuesday and Friday 07:45 - 12:00, during your long day you will be entitled to an hour unpaid lunch break. You will also be required to work some occasional additional shifts (possibly half days) to cover holiday / sickness. To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, the processing of information and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multi-disciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The following are the core responsibilities of the Receptionist. There may be, on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks. This will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: a. Maintain and monitor the practice appointment system b. Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments c. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately d. Signpost patients to the correct service e. Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies f. Clinically code data on SystmOne g. Photocopy documentation as required h. Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as required i. Input data into patients healthcare records as necessary j. Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner k. Maintain a clean, tidy, effective working area at all times l. Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards m. Support all clinical staff with general tasks as requested n. Provide cover during staff absences o. Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary p. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the duty rota q. Produce, maintain and participate in the receptionist rota for lunch and out of hours cover

title: Team Administrator
description: This is an opportunity to join one of our friendly TALKWORKS teams, with two opportunities available: one with the East Devon TALKWORKS team, based in Exeter, and the other with the Mid Devon TALKWORKS team, based at Tiverton Hospital. Both roles offer hybrid working, including the option to work from home on some days if required. The post holder will need a good telephone manner, as the role involves responding to clients phoning into the service, and processing referrals, and making calls to clients. The role also therefore requires the accurate entry of confidential and sensitive data into clinical record systems. The role will involve the coordination and implementation of office procedures and will require a high degree of organisational skills and excellent working knowledge of administrative systems. Interviews for these posts are scheduled to take place on Tuesday 20th October at Elizabeth House in Exeter. If you are applying for the Tiverton based post and travelling to Exeter for the interview would be problematic please contact the recruiting manager to discuss alternative options. Duties and Responsibilities Key Responsibilities include: Work within the friendly Exeter and East or Mid Devon administration team supporting clinicians who provide psychological therapy Comprehensive diary management Meetings administration; taking and distributing formal minutes; recording clear actions. Frequently inputting complex and sensitive data relating to people who use our services onto electronic patient records system Support the manager and team by ensuring that records are up to date on all staffing and patient systems and that items are dealt with quickly and efficiently. The Job description can be viewed in the attached document. This also covers the person specification.

title: Service Administrator
company: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
description: Providing excellent customer service to patients, colleagues, and multidisciplinary teams in line with Trust values and standards. Coordinating and organising patient attendance for surgeries, pre-ops and outpatient appointments. Ensuring all administrative processes and patient enquiries are managed efficiently and within required timescales. Delivering a comprehensive secretarial and administrative service to Consultants, nursing teams, and the wider team. Producing accurate, professional documentation to a high standard with strong attention to detail and proofreading skills. Monitoring patients waiting lists (outpatient and surgical) and ensuring compliance with NHS targets and Trust standards. Managing telephone, email, and written correspondence professionally and effectively. Supporting service continuity by working collaboratively with colleagues and ensuring adequate cover during periods of leave. Adhering to governance, compliance, and mandatory training requirements in line with Trust policies. For more detail about the main duties of this role, please see the job description section below. As a key member of the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, you will be joining an exceptional team working together to help our patients to stay healthy, when they need it most. For more information on the Job Description and Responsibilities please click the link below. More detail about the role We are looking for an enthusiastic, motivated and dedicated Service Administrator to join our busy Ophthalmology Department. The successful candidate will be highly organised and motivated, with excellent communication and interpersonal skills. You will be able to prioritise and manage your workload effectively, work calmly under pressure, and thrive in a busy and varied working environment. A positive, flexible and proactive approach is essential, along with a commitment to providing a high-quality administrative service to patients and colleagues. The post holder will ideally have previous administrative experience, preferably within a secretarial or healthcare setting. However, we also welcome applications from candidates with experience in other sectors who can demonstrate relevant and transferable skills. This is a challenging yet rewarding role, offering the opportunity to become an integral part of a dedicated Ophthalmology team. If you feel you have the skills, enthusiasm and commitment to meet the demands of the role, we would be delighted to hear from you. Visits to the department are warmly welcomed and encouraged. If you would like to arrange a visit or find out more about the role, please contact the Team Leader using the details provided below. Working Pattern: Monday - Friday, 09:00-17:00 - 37.5 hours Interview Date: Wednesday 14th October For further information please contact: Charlotte Hornby, Team Leader on charlotte.hornby3@nhs.net This is a fixed term contract for 12 months. For current NHS employees this post could be a secondment opportunity. As an inclusive employer, the Royal Devon values diversity and is committed to creating a culture of inclusivity where everyone can be themselves and reach their full potential. We believe in fostering a sense of belonging and actively encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, cultures, and abilities. We recognise the advantages of having a diverse workforce that reflects the communities we serve. Preference will be given to staff with Priority and 'At Risk' status including NHS At Risk staff throughout Devon. The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust reserves the right to close vacancy when sufficient applications have been received. The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust was established in April 2022, bringing together the expertise of both the Royal Devon and Exeter NHS Foundation Trust and Northern Devon Healthcare NHS Trust. Benefits We will work together to maintain a culture that develops and supports you and your team. This might include funding for a care certificate, a degree or leadership qualifications. Or it might include days off to study, engage in CPD or rotational placements to help you hone your skills. Wherever you are heading in the NHS, we'll help you get there. Looking after you is important to us. We strive to help our staff create a healthy work-life balance through flexible working schemes and our family friendly policies. If you're starting out in the NHS, you'll start with 27 days paid annual leave (plus bank holidays), rising to 33 days plus bank holidays. You'll benefit from access to our own comprehensive occupational health services, including counselling, onsite wellbeing activities and groups. Salary is not the only financial benefit You'll have access to an extensive range of staff discounts on shopping, fitness and leisure options and you can spread the cost of technology and home appliance purchases from major retailers. You will also have access to other benefits including: National discount services such as the Blue Light Card and Health Service Discounts. Salary sacrifice options including our OFSTED rated outstanding nursery onsite at Exeter Car lease schemes. The NHS Pension scheme (one of the most generous and comprehensive in the UK). Cycle to work scheme These are just a few of the benefits available if the role is something you are interested in, we'd love to hear from you.
